name: Thymeleaf SSTI via expression preprocessing or user-controlled fragment
attack_scenario: Attacker sets section=__${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('id')}__ (or the fragment renders a __${...}__ payload); Thymeleaf preprocesses and evaluates the SpEL, executing arbitrary code on the server.
negative_test_hint: submit section = "__${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('id')}__" and assert it is treated as a plain fragment name or rejected, never evaluated as a SpEL expression

exemplar.explanation: Thymeleaf's __${...}__ preprocessing double-evaluates the inner expression, and a controller that returns a fragment selector ('view :: fragment') concatenated with user input lets Thymeleaf evaluate that input as a SpEL expression; both are direct SSTI-to-RCE vectors. Returning a fixed, developer-chosen fragment keeps user data out of template selection, so no attacker string is ever parsed as an expression.
